solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thinking the French court needs to get flipping finger out

indicators.note: the shuffled finger has to go out, on the outside, with the other pieces held within it
flipping in its sense of tossing over and over, so the word finger is jumbled

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A judge in a French courtroom wants someone to stop making a rude gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' is the anagram signal (as in tossing over), not the British mild curse; 'out' means the jumbled letters sit outside the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflecting on something is pondering it, so the participle is a synonym for thinking.

clue.text: Bit of a shock, damaged lips getting treated by nurse

definitions.note: a shock here is a mass of hair, and a frayed tip is one small piece of it

indicators.note: damaged suggests a broken form, so the word lips is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: An electric shock has left someone's lips hurt, and a nurse is patching them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' means a thick head of hair, not a jolt; 'damaged' rearranges LIPS into SPLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A frayed hair tip is a tiny part of a shock, meaning a head of hair: definition by example.

clue.text: Put fork into fish sample

indicators.note: the clue says to put one piece into another, so the fork goes inside the fish

parts.note: a trout is a freshwater fish
Y is shaped like a fork, a common crossword device

explanation.surface: An instruction to stick a fork in a piece of fish and taste it.
explanation.walkthrough: Y stands for 'fork' because of its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run or test performance is a sample of what someone or something can do.

clue.text: Newspaper in topless tabloid model's hand?

indicators.note: the newspaper goes in, placed inside the other letters
topless means the top letter is removed from the tabloid

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
the Model T was an early Ford car
the i is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid's topless page-three model holding a newspaper in her hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter of the tabloid. The i and The Sun are British papers; the Model T was an early Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a measure of four inches used for horse heights, so it is an example of a measuring standard.

clue.text: Fake that initially can lead to gallery not showing "The Persistence of Memory"

parts.note: to fake a document or painting is to forge it

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of that

parts.note: a can is a tin
the lead, or leading letter, of the word gallery is G

explanation.surface: A forger's fake gets into a gallery that doesn't actually exhibit Dalí's famous melting-clocks painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Persistence of Memory is Dalí's melting-clocks painting; the puzzle's clues name his works throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing recall is the opposite of memory persisting, so failing to show the painting's title doubles as the lapse.

clue.text: Leaders of gang sporting top jewellery? One of them must be on the fiddle

definitions.text: One of them must be on the fiddle
definitions.note: a violin carries strings tuned G, D, A, E, so the lowest of them is always present; the definition is singular for a plural answer

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the next three words

parts.note: rings are items of jewellery

explanation.surface: A gang wearing flashy jewellery, with one of them always up to some fiddle or swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fiddle' is a violin, not a swindle: its lowest string is tuned to G.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin's lowest strings are tuned to G, so a fiddle always has one; the skimpy-underwear sense also lurks.

clue.text: Crying? No time for reprimand

indicators.note: no time means the time letter is missing

parts.note: someone crying is tearful

explanation.surface: Someone in tears is told there is no time for that, which itself is a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A long scolding given to someone is a reprimand: an informal synonym.

clue.text: Frenchwoman's S & M set-up

parts.note: the letter S is spelt out as ES

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: the letter M is spelt out as EM

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's kinky bondage arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: S and M are taken as letter names, ES and EM; 'set-up' turns EM into ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the name as French in origin, so a girl bearing it can be called a Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Repeats "No bad language"

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters are in a wrong, spoiled order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone keeps telling others not to use bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad language' wants to be the definition, but 'bad' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the invented international auxiliary tongue devised by Zamenhof.

clue.text: Swimmers that fly with a small number on board

indicators.note: to be on board is to be inside the vessel, so on places the pieces within the ship's letters

parts.note: the board one goes on here is a steamship, abbreviated SS
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Waterfowl flying with a few of their number riding aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' places the pieces inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: These big white waterbirds both glide on water and take to the air: definition by description.

clue.text: Hob needs help in getting prepared for burial

indicators.note: help goes in, placed within the other word

parts.note: a hob is an old word for a rustic clown or lout; also the setter's own pseudonym
aid is help

explanation.surface: The setter, Hob, needs help getting ready to be buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hob' looks like the setter's name but means a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse that has been washed and arranged before a funeral is said to have been made ready this way.

clue.text: Topless show, with boobs endlessly out — it shows some neck

indicators.note: out means on the outside, so the blunders go around the other piece
endlessly means the last letter of the blunders is dropped

parts.note: boobs are blunders, gaffes

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: to air something is to show it

explanation.surface: A topless revue, boobs on display, that shows a lot of flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boobs' means blunders here; 'Topless' and 'endlessly' trim the front of one word and the end of the other before 'out' wraps one around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall African animal is famous for its long neck, so it displays plenty of one: a playful description.

clue.text: Surrealistic? He's totally in that box

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across the end of one word and the next

explanation.surface: A surreal question about a man entirely shut inside a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Surrealistic' across 'He's' into 'totally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large lidded wooden container is a box: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Gets involved in complications if folk-jazz band's dropping piano intro

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is removed from the band's name

parts.note: Pentangle was a British folk-jazz band of the late 1960s; the 's adds an S

indicators.note: the intro of piano is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A folk-jazz band complicates matters by cutting the piano introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Pentangle were a British folk-jazz group; the possessive supplies the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare someone in difficulties or a tangle is to involve them in complications.

clue.text: Starting exile in Saint-Denis, desperately missing one northern part of Asia

indicators.note: starting means the first letter of exile
desperately suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged
missing means one letter is taken out before rearranging

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern; Saint-Denis has two, and only one goes

explanation.surface: An exile starting a new life in the Paris suburb of Saint-Denis, desperately missing home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing one northern' drops one of the two Ns from SAINT-DENIS; 'desperately' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for the islands of South-East Asia, such as the Malay archipelago, names a region of that continent.

clue.text: Call girl up, one into herself not love — after a bit of sex, in general?

indicators.note: after means the other pieces follow this letter
a bit of sex is its opening letter
up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tart is slang for a call girl

indicators.note: not means a letter is left out

parts.note: someone wrapped up in themselves is an egoist
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed call girl who, after a little sex, wants nothing to do with love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TART into TRAT; 'not love' drops O from EGOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a military commander who plans campaigns, so is an expert planner.

clue.text: Treats with element of suspicion, essentially

definitions.text: Treats with element of suspicion, essentially

parts.words: Treats with element of suspicion, essentially
parts.note: the element at the heart of the word suspicion is its middle letter I, the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Someone regards things warily, at bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'suspicion' is I, the symbol for iodine, so treating with that element means adding iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding iodine, as to table salt, is the chemical treatment the verb names.

clue.text: "Soft Construction with Boiled Beans"? Not adult enough for gathering of stuck-up people

indicators.note: boiled suggests cooking into a new mess, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: not means the adult letter is taken away

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: Dalí's painting Soft Construction with Boiled Beans, judged not mature enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The painting's title supplies SOFT and BEANS; 'Not adult' drops A, and 'Boiled' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An event full of snooty people is a festival of snobbery: informal compound.

clue.text: Mental nurse in state about Churchill?

definitions.note: Churchill is a British firm that sells cover against loss, with a nodding bulldog mascot

indicators.note: the jumbled nurse goes in, inside the state's letters
about means the state's abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a US state

indicators.note: mental suggests a disturbed state, so the letters of nurse are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse in a psychiatric ward, worked up about Winston Churchill.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill here is a British insurance company, not Winston. 'about' turns RI to IR; 'Mental' shuffles NURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill is a well-known UK firm offering policies against loss, so it is an example of an underwriter.

clue.text: "Metamorphosis of Narcissus", lacking a bit of colour in what once were reds?

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a change of form, so the letters of Narcissus are transformed
lacking means one letter is taken out
a bit of colour is its first letter

explanation.surface: Dalí's Metamorphosis of Narcissus, seen as lacking a touch of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a bit of colour' drops C from NARCISSUS before 'Metamorphosis of' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Communists of the Soviet era were nicknamed Reds, and the people of the USSR were thus called.

clue.text: Moving fast as Lassie, bounding along

parts.note: a lassie is a girl or gal
loping is moving with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: Lassie the film collie racing along at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lassie' looks like the famous dog but is just a girl, GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Running at a horse's fastest pace means going at speed: a synonym.

clue.text: Advanced in slowly, or fast, with nothing shed

indicators.note: the advanced letter goes in, inside the musical term

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Someone advancing at a crawl, or else quickly, owning nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers a second route: A inside LENT (fast) plus O (nothing). 'shed' looks like a verb but names a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple sloping-roofed hut built against a wall is a kind of outbuilding or shed.

clue.text: Surround source of sugar, surrounded by source of sugar

indicators.note: the first piece is surrounded, so it goes within the second

parts.note: sugar beet is a major source of sugar

indicators.note: the source of sugar is its first letter

explanation.surface: A word game repeating the same phrase, one source of sugar wrapped in another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of sugar' is read two ways: the first letter S, and BEET.
explanation.definitionFit: To beleaguer or hem in on all sides is to surround: a synonym.

clue.text: Girl drunk in the bar

indicators.note: drunk suggests a staggering, disordered state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl who has had too much to drink in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like it describes the girl but shuffles THE BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's first name, so any bearer of it is a girl: an example.

clue.text: Happy, perhaps, before party leader's made to look small

parts.note: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White
Ed Miliband led the UK Labour Party when this was published

explanation.surface: A cheerful politician is put before the party leader and diminished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs. Ed Miliband was the UK Labour leader in 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overshadowed by something larger is to be made to seem tiny: a synonym.

clue.text: 11 in Dublin house

parts.note: 11 across is the phrase 'laid out', read here as wordplay: the four letters of laid, with out as the instruction to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A cross-reference placing another answer in Ireland's parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is LAID OUT: its first word supplies the letters and its second is the anagram signal, so one clue number does both jobs. The same letters also make DALI, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower chamber of the Irish parliament, sitting in Dublin, is a legislative house.

clue.text: Hot food that's eaten at home round about noon

indicators.note: the food has the other letters eaten, taken inside it
round about means the whole assembly is turned back to front

parts.note: grub is slang for food
in means at home

explanation.surface: Lunchtime hot food eaten at home around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUB eats NIN to make GNINRUB, which 'round about' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire or scorching to the touch is very hot: a synonym.

clue.text: Second letter — second part of official complaint

parts.note: B is the second letter of the alphabet, spelt out as bee

indicators.note: the second part, or second letter, of the word official

explanation.surface: A formal letter, the second of a series, forming part of an official complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: B is spelt out as BEE; the 'second part of official' is its second letter, F.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal grievance or gripe is slang for a complaint.

clue.text: Stroke some gigantic tusks

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An elephant's huge tusks delivering a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine and prosody the Latin term means a seizure or a rhythmic beat, a sudden blow.

clue.text: Lethe? Snap out of it, maybe they'll never be 5

indicators.note: out of it means dazed or befuddled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written; Lethe is the river of forgetfulness
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drinker from Lethe, the river of forgetfulness, is told to snap out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is FORGETTING: the saying goes that these animals never forget. 'out of it' shuffles LETHE SNAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially these big animals have long memories, so they are never forgetful: a playful idiom.
